CLAUDE.md

This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.

Overview

async is an R package that brings asynchronous computation and I/O to R. It provides an event loop that schedules async functions whose results are reported via deferred values (promises/futures). Deferred values can be chained and are evaluated lazily, at synchronisation points.

Common commands

This is a standard R package developed with devtools/testthat (edition 3).

# Load the package for interactive development
uncovr::reload()

# Run the full test suite
uncovr::test()

# Run a single test file (by filename fragment, no "test-" prefix or ".R")
uncovr::test(filter = "http")          # runs tests/testthat/test-http.R

# Documentation (roxygen2 -> man/, NAMESPACE)
uncovr::document()

# R CMD check
withr::with_envvar(c(NOT_CRAN = "true", DISPLAY = NA), rcmdcheck::rcmdcheck())
# Regenerate README.md from README.Rmd (the only Makefile target)
make

Documentation is roxygen-based (Roxygen: list(markdown = TRUE, r6 = FALSE)). Note r6 = FALSE: R6 classes are documented manually in @section blocks, not auto-generated — see R/deferred.R for the pattern.

Testing notes

  • Tests requiring an HTTP server use a local webfakes httpbin instance started in tests/testthat/setup-httpbin.R (the http process object). Reference it as http$url(...) inside tests — do not hit real external hosts.
  • skip_without_package() and get_private(x) (to reach an R6 object’s private env) are defined in tests/testthat/helper.R.
  • Snapshot tests live in tests/testthat/_snaps/.

Architecture

The package is built from three interlocking concepts. Understanding them together is essential before changing core behaviour.

1. Deferred values (R/deferred.R)

A deferred is an R6 object representing a value that is not yet known. It is the basic building block for everything else. Key design points:

  • Strong ownership: each deferred has exactly one child that receives its result (or error). Attaching a second child, or reusing an already-owned parent, is an error. $share() opts out of this for fan-out.
  • A deferred is constructed with an action (run when the deferred is started, not when created) plus parents and parent_resolve/parent_reject callbacks that fire as parents resolve/reject. See the long roxygen block at the top of the file for the full contract, including the shorthand forms accepted for parent_resolve/parent_reject.
  • Combinators build on this: $then(), $catch(), $finally(), and the top-level when_all() / when_any() / when_some().

2. Synchronisation barriers (R/synchronise.R)

Execution alternates between a sync phase and async phases. You cannot create/evaluate deferred values in the sync phase — you enter an async phase by calling synchronise(expr), which:

  • Pushes a fresh event loop, evaluates expr, and if the result is a deferred, runs the loop until it resolves (or rejects, re-throwing the error).
  • Cancels all outstanding async work on exit, interrupt, or external error.
  • Enforces the barrier: a deferred chain cannot cross a synchronise() boundary. Loops can be nested (an inner synchronise() pauses the outer loop).

Lazy evaluation + auto-cancellation are consequences of this model: only deferreds needed to compute the synchronised result are started, and ones no longer needed are cancelled as soon as possible.

3. Event loop (R/event-loop.R)

An R6 event_loop class whose methods are thin wrappers delegating to free functions named el_* (public) and el__* (private) in the same file. It integrates several I/O sources into one poll loop:

  • HTTP via curl multi handles (add_http)
  • external processes and R subprocesses via processx (add_process, add_r_process)
  • a worker pool of persistent R processes (add_pool_task, see R/worker-pool.R)
  • timers / delayed callbacks (add_delayed) and add_next_tick

When editing loop behaviour, add the method stub in the R6Class definition and implement the corresponding el_*/el__* function.

Async primitives and helpers

The async I/O constructors that produce deferreds: delay() (R/delay.R), http_get()/http_head() (R/http.R, R/http-sse.R), run_process() (R/process.R), run_r_process() (R/r-process.R), and call_function() (worker pool). async() (R/aaa-async.R) wraps a plain function into one that returns a deferred (it rewrites the function body — see the bquote transformation).

Collection-style helpers built on the combinators live in files named after them: async_map() (R/map.R), async_detect(), async_filter(), async_some(), async_race(), retry/backoff, timeout, etc.

Dependencies (from DESCRIPTION): callr, curl, processx, R6, utils.
